- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 1–3% from next 3–5 forecast points.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.0) within 5 days, model overreacts to short-term volatility; dampen forecast decline by 1–3% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.0–0.5); add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to align with historical mean.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend if sentiment is trending.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model starts with high value (e.g., >85) and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce first 3–5 points by 2–4% to avoid over-optimism.
- If true outcome shows early sharp drop after high peak, model often fails to anticipate; add 1–2% downward bias in 3–5 forecast points following peak.
